content: Sleepeating, also known as Nocturnal Eating Syndrome, is classified as a parasomnia, a type of sleep disorder. It is characterized by recurrent episodes of eating during sleep, with the individual having no conscious awareness of their actions. These episodes can occur frequently enough to lead to significant weight gain over time. This condition can affect individuals of all ages and genders, but it is observed more commonly in young women. In Australia, the medication Ambien, marketed under the name Stilnox, has been associated with side effects such as sleepdriving and sleepeating, as reported by the Australian drug regulatory agency. During sleepeating episodes, individuals may repeatedly consume the same food multiple times throughout the night. This behavior often involves several trips to the refrigerator or cupboard until the desired food item is completely consumed. Certain medications and the consumption of alcohol can increase the likelihood of sleepwalking and related behaviors, such as sleepeating, in individuals who are predisposed to these episodes.
